title: Tag-range filtering for gitpulse: --since-tag / --until-tag across all CLI paths
essence: Prior to this initiative gitpulse had no way to scope analytics to the commits between two version tags; users had to translate tag names to dates manually and accept date-boundary imprecision. The change introduces resolveTagToSha (commit-SHA resolution via git rev-parse --verify <tag>^{commit}, handling both annotated and lightweight tags) and filterCommitsByTagRange (a pure, no-git-spawn array slicer with exclusive lower / inclusive upper semantics), then wires --since-tag / --until-tag through all four CLI paths (single-snapshot, --compare, coupling, tags), extends text/JSON/CSV renderers with range annotations, and proves the whole chain in a self-contained acceptance fixture with a deterministic Charles Babbage repo.

bullets: New src/tag-range.ts: resolveTagToSha resolves any tag (annotated or lightweight) to its underlying commit SHA via git rev-parse --verify <tag>^{commit}; unknown tags exit 2 with all known tags listed newest-first.
filterCommitsByTagRange is a pure array slicer (no git spawn): since-tag is the exclusive lower bound, until-tag is the inclusive upper bound; inverted and empty ranges return [] without error.
resolveEffectiveBounds merges --since-tag with a --since date, picking whichever is narrower and annotating the header with which bound won.
src/cli.ts wires the two flags through all four paths (single-snapshot, --compare, coupling subcommand, tags subcommand); the tags subcommand explicitly rejects them with exit 2.
src/format.ts extends text, JSON, and CSV renderers with range annotations that persist even when the filtered commit set is empty.

test/acceptance/run.ts builds a fresh Charles Babbage fixture repo (annotated v1.0.0 on PRE, lightweight v2.0.0 on INTER-2, POST after) and asserts 7 scenarios end-to-end against the real built dist/cli.js.
README.md documents --since-tag and --until-tag in the global flags table with exclusive/inclusive boundary rules.

checkpoints.label: resolveTagToSha: annotated and lightweight tags both return commit SHA
checkpoints.caption: git rev-parse --verify <tag>^{commit} unwraps both tag-object and direct-commit refs; the unit tests in test/tag-range.test.ts verify the pure logic, while the acceptance fixture exercises the real git binary.
checkpoints.beforeNote: No resolveTagToSha existed; callers had to resolve tags manually and could silently get a tag-object SHA instead of a commit SHA, breaking SHA-equality checks.
checkpoints.afterNote: resolveTagToSha always returns the underlying commit SHA. For annotated tags (tag-object SHA ≠ commit SHA) and lightweight tags (tag SHA = commit SHA) alike the result is the commit SHA. Unknown tags throw { code: 2, unknownTag, knownTags } with the full sorted known-tag list.

checkpoints.afterNote: Single-snapshot: --since-tag v1.0.0 excludes the tagged commit and all older commits; --until-tag v2.0.0 includes the tagged commit and excludes newer ones; both together define a precise window. All three renderers emit the range annotation even when the window yields zero commits.

usage_example:
# Single-snapshot: commits strictly after v1.0.0 tag
gitpulse . --since-tag v1.0.0

# Bounded window: commits after v1.0.0 up to and including v2.0.0
gitpulse . --since-tag v1.0.0 --until-tag v2.0.0

# JSON output with range metadata
gitpulse . --since-tag v1.0.0 --until-tag v2.0.0 --json
# → { ..., "range": { "sinceTag": "v1.0.0", "untilTag": "v2.0.0", "sinceSha": "<sha>", "untilSha": "<sha>" } }

# CSV output with range header comment
gitpulse . --since-tag v1.0.0 --until-tag v2.0.0 --csv
# → # range: v1.0.0..v2.0.0 (sinceSha:<sha>, untilSha:<sha>)
# → Author,Commits,...

# Compose with --compare for delta analytics between tag boundaries
gitpulse . --since-tag v1.0.0 --until-tag v2.0.0 --compare main

# Compose with coupling subcommand
gitpulse coupling . --since-tag v1.0.0 --until-tag v2.0.0

# Narrow conflicting date and tag bounds — narrower wins with annotation
gitpulse . --since-tag v1.0.0 --since 2024-03-01
impact: Teams can now scope all gitpulse analytics (summary, compare delta, coupling, ownership, hotspots) to an exact tag-bounded release window — no more manual SHA lookups or imprecise date translations.
Both annotated and lightweight tags are resolved correctly to the underlying commit SHA, so tag type is transparent to the user.
An inverted or empty range is graceful: zero commits are returned (not an error), and all three output renderers (text, JSON, CSV) still emit the range annotation so the boundary intent is visible.
The tags subcommand explicitly rejects --since-tag / --until-tag with exit 2 and a clear message, preventing silent misuse.
The --since and --since-tag flags compose intelligently: whichever bound is narrower wins, and the header annotation names which bound was applied.

acEvaluations.criterion: GIVEN a repo with an annotated tag v1.0.0 (tag object SHA ≠ commit SHA) and a lightweight tag v2.0.0 (tag SHA = commit SHA) WHEN resolveTagToSha(repoPath, 'v1.0.0') and resolveTagToSha(repoPath, 'v2.0.0') are called THEN both return the underlying commit SHA (via git rev-parse --verify <tag>^{commit}), not the tag-object SHA
acEvaluations.evidence: src/git.ts resolveTagToSha() uses execFileSync('git', ['-C', repoPath, 'rev-parse', '--verify', `${tag}^{commit}`]) which unwraps tag objects to commit SHAs for both annotated and lightweight tags. The acceptance fixture at test/acceptance/run.ts line 395 uses gitOut(['rev-parse', `${TAG_RANGE_SENTINEL_V1}^{commit}`]) to capture v1Sha (annotated) and line 409 for v2Sha (lightweight), then asserts in AC3 that range.sinceSha === capturedV1Sha and range.untilSha === capturedV2Sha.

acEvaluations.criterion: GIVEN a repo with tags v1.0.0, v0.9.0, v0.8.0 and no tag v99.0.0 WHEN resolveTagToSha(repoPath, 'v99.0.0') is called THEN it throws an error carrying exit code 2, the unknown tag name verbatim (including dots), and a sorted list of all known tags newest-first (v1.0.0, v0.9.0, v0.8.0)
acEvaluations.evidence: src/git.ts resolveTagToSha() catch block sets err.code = 2, err.unknownTag = tag, err.knownTags = knownTags.map(t => t.name), and the error message includes the verbatim tag name and the sorted list from readTags(). The acceptance test AC7 in run.ts asserts: exit code 2 AND stderr contains TAG_RANGE_SENTINEL_V1 / TAG_RANGE_SENTINEL_V2 AND references 'vNONE'. The cli-tag-range.test.ts 'unknown --since-tag exits 2 with unknown tag name in message' test also asserts result.code === 2 and result.stderr.includes('vNONE').
